tasks.title: Establish the verify-only egress baseline and warn-closed boot wiring
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-4 (openspec/changes/sbx-4-sbx-network-and-secrets) defines Dune's sbx egress posture. The sbx-3 backend already exists: internal/dune/runtime/sbx/{backend.go,lifecycle.go,validate.go,runner.go} with the D5 command-runner seam (Runner.Capture/Stream, fakeRunner in runner_test.go). app.go wires commands through dispatchRuntimeCommand / runUp (internal/dune/app.go:141-187), calling Validate -> Ensure -> Status -> Start -> Shell. Design D1 and task 1.4 (already resolved by spike 4, struck through in tasks.md) settled that NO sandbox-scoped preset exists: `sbx policy set-default` is global-only and `sbx policy profile` lists only remote-governance profiles. Therefore Dune takes the VERIFY-ONLY path: never apply a preset, never mutate global policy, never weaken to Open.

Outcome: a backend capability that reads the active egress posture for an instance (via `sbx policy ls`, sandbox-scoped where the flag exists) and classifies it as Open vs non-Open, plus boot-time wiring so `up`/Ensure: (a) never sets the posture to Open on the user's behalf; (b) never mutates the user's global sbx default policy/profile; (c) warns CLOSED with an actionable message (how to set a non-Open posture) when a non-Open posture cannot be confirmed, WITHOUT hard-failing (the global default may already be non-Open); (d) hard-fails only when it positively observes an Open posture it was asked to operate under. This matches D1's split between the up-time behavior and the read-only doctor check (the doctor check itself is sbx-5; here only the inspection primitive + up-time warn-closed).

Files & scope: add to internal/dune/runtime/sbx (new method(s) on Backend/backend, e.g. a posture-inspection method + the decision logic) constructing `sbx policy ls` through the runner seam; wire the warn-closed message into the up/Ensure path in internal/dune/app.go (or runtime) without changing the existing Validate/Status/Start/Shell sequencing semantics. Do not implement allow/deny/open-domain here (that is the next lap). Do not add the final `dune logs`/`dune doctor` composition (sbx-5).

Design: keep concrete sbx command shapes private to the sbx package (matches backend.go's stated convention). Reconfirm the `sbx policy ls` flag/output shape via `sbx policy ls --help` before pinning; parse defensively (the spikes used `--json` for some policy commands). The warn-closed vs hard-fail distinction is the subtle, security-relevant judgment — get it exactly per D1: unconfirmable => warn (proceed), positively-Open-when-asked-to-operate => fail. Surface the warning on stderr through the existing streams plumbing.

Acceptance: fakeRunner tests pin the `sbx policy ls` argument construction and assert the classify/decision logic across the three cases (confirmed non-Open => proceed quietly; unconfirmable => warn-closed, proceed, actionable message; observed Open => fail). `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./internal/dune/...` green. Report the exact warn/fail messages emitted.

tasks.title: Build sandbox-scoped egress-rule construction and the domain-opening rule shape
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-4 design D2/D3. Spikes verified the rule shapes (design.md D2 code block): `sbx policy allow network --sandbox <instance> <domain>:443`, `sbx policy deny network --sandbox <instance> <domain>`, `sbx policy rm network --sandbox <instance> --resource <domain>:443`. <instance> is the `dune-<slug>-<profile>` sandbox name from sbx-3 D3 (Spec.InstanceName). The positional `--sandbox` form was rejected in spike 3 — use the `--sandbox <name>` flag form. Builds on the previous lap's posture-inspection; reuses the same runner seam.

Outcome: backend methods (kept in the sbx package) that apply Dune-managed egress rules SCOPED to the instance's sandbox: allow a domain, deny a domain, and remove a rule (removal via `--resource <domain>:443`). A domain-opening affordance at the backend level that, when opening a project domain, adds BOTH the exact domain and a specific wildcard when both are needed (`example.org` and `*.example.org` are independent per spike 3), and PREFERS exact + specific-wildcard rules over broad catch-alls (`**.amazonaws.com`-style). Rules are sandbox-scoped (never touch global policy) and take effect immediately on the running sandbox.

Files & scope: internal/dune/runtime/sbx (new methods + the exact/wildcard pairing helper) constructing the verified `sbx policy allow/deny/rm` shapes through the runner seam. Do NOT introduce a new top-level `dune` verb — D3 fixes the rule shape and behavior only; the user-facing command name (a `dune` wrapper vs documented `sbx policy allow` guidance) is coordinated with the command set finalised in sbx-5. Do not implement `sbx policy log` here (next lap).

Design: reconfirm flags via `sbx policy --help` before use (design notes flags may drift across versions). Keep the exact-vs-wildcard logic explicit and testable. Default `:443` port on the allow/exact form per the spike-verified shape, but make the construction assertable.

Acceptance: fakeRunner tests pin the EXACT argument vectors for allow (`allow network --sandbox <instance> <domain>:443`), deny (`deny network --sandbox <instance> <domain>`), and rm (`rm network --sandbox <instance> --resource <domain>:443`), plus a test showing the domain-opening affordance emits both the exact and the specific-wildcard rule when both are requested and never emits a broad catch-all. This satisfies the rule-construction portion of task 6.1. `go test ./internal/dune/...` green.

tasks.title: Wrap sbx policy log as the egress observability source
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-4 design D4 / tasks 3.1, 3.2. `sbx policy log <instance>` is the first-class egress observability source replacing `dune logs pipelock`. Spike 4 confirmed a structured form: `sbx policy log [SANDBOX] --json` with `--limit int` and `--type all|network` (sandbox name is positional and optional). The existing interim `Logs` method (internal/dune/runtime/sbx/lifecycle.go:90) tails `/var/log/dune/*.log` and has NO pipelock service — this lap ADDS a new policy-log wrapper, it does not modify that interim Logs. The final `dune logs` composition (policy log + Dune-owned logs) is sbx-5, not this change.

Outcome: a backend method (sbx package) that wraps `sbx policy log <instance> --json` (supporting `--limit`) through the sbx-3 runner seam, parsing the structured records into a typed shape. Field names are pinned from observed output so a future sbx output change surfaces as a test failure (mirroring the existing convention noted at validate.go:62).

Files & scope: internal/dune/runtime/sbx (new method + a small record struct + parse). Construct via the runner seam (Capture for the `--json` form). Do not compose `dune logs` end-to-end (sbx-5).

Design: follow the existing sbx-package patterns (see Status/parseSandboxList in lifecycle.go for JSON-shape-tolerant parsing). Reconfirm the flag surface via `sbx policy log --help` before pinning. Covers both `forward` (direct shell) and `transparent` (nested Docker) record types per the spikes — the parse must not assume a single type.

Acceptance: fakeRunner test pins the `sbx policy log <instance> --json --limit <n>` invocation and asserts the parsed field names against a recorded sample (including a transparent/nested-Docker record). This completes the policy-log portion of task 6.1. `go test ./internal/dune/...` green.

tasks.title: Implement the v1 secrets posture and service-secret construction helpers
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-4 design D5 / tasks 4.1, 4.2, 4.3. The v1 decision is already made in the design: PREFER service-identifier secrets; treat custom secrets as experimental/out-of-lifecycle; no secrets in the template; agent-provider creds stay in the profile-scoped /persist/agent location (sbx-3 D3) until a built-in agent or kit declares a service identifier. Note: in v1 no core boot path actually sets a service secret — these helpers are a forward-looking, tested surface, not yet wired into `up`.

Outcome: service-secret construction helpers (sbx package) for set/ls/rm built through the sbx-3 runner seam, with the verified spike-3 shapes pinned: `sbx secret set <instance> <service> -t <ENV_VAR>`, `sbx secret ls <instance>`, `sbx secret rm <instance> <service> -f` (the scope is the dune-<slug>-<profile> instance name). A code-level assertion/guard (and/or test) that no core Dune boot path depends on `sbx secret set-custom`.

Files & scope: internal/dune/runtime/sbx (helpers + tests). Do not wire these into the up/Ensure boot path (none is required in v1). Documentation of the posture lands in the later docs lap, not here.

Design: reconfirm via `sbx secret --help` before pinning (flags may drift). Mirror the runner-seam construction pattern from the egress laps. Custom secrets (set-custom) are explicitly out of v1 lifecycle ownership — do not build a lifecycle around them.

Acceptance: fakeRunner tests pin the exact set/ls/rm argument vectors, completing the service-secret portion of task 6.1. A test (or the absence, demonstrable) confirms no boot path invokes set-custom. `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./internal/dune/...` green.

tasks.title: Complete Pipelock removal (sequenced after the egress baseline)
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-4 design D6 / tasks 5.1-5.4. PLANNING NOTE (confirm, do not re-discover): sbx-3's Compose removal already excised the Pipelock call sites, the `ensurePipelockConfig` function, the proxy-env (HTTP(S)_PROXY) injection, and the `dune logs pipelock` surface. A current `grep -rn pipelock|Pipelock|HTTP_PROXY|HTTPS_PROXY internal/ --include=*.go` matches ONLY files inside internal/dune/pipelock/ itself (pipelock.go, pipelock_test.go) — the package is present-but-unused, referenced only by itself, and nothing in app.go imports it. The interim Logs (lifecycle.go:90) tails /var/log/dune/*.log with no pipelock service. So the residual removal is: delete the self-contained package and confirm the rest is already gone.

Ordering gate (D6): this lap runs only after the egress policy surface has landed and been verified (the prior VERIFY lap), so sbx policy governs egress for the sbx path before the last Pipelock code is deleted — there is no window where egress is both un-proxied and un-policed. Pipelock is NOT the active egress mediator on the sbx path (sbx-3 already stopped starting it), so deleting the dead package does not change runtime egress behavior; still, honor the sequencing.

Outcome: `internal/dune/pipelock/` (pipelock.go, pipelock.yaml.tmpl, pipelock_test.go, and the testdata directory) is deleted; a fresh repo-wide grep confirms no remaining references to pipelock / the proxy-env model / a `dune logs pipelock` surface anywhere outside archived openspec material; the build and tests stay green.

Files & scope: delete internal/dune/pipelock/ in full. Verify (and only if found, remove) any stray reference elsewhere. Do not touch the legacy Compose backend on main — Pipelock remains there; this removal is for the dunex sbx path only. Do not rewrite git history.

Design: before deleting, run the grep gate and confirm the call sites/proxy-env/`dune logs pipelock` surface are already absent (per the planning note); judge that removing the package leaves no dangling import or build break. This is a removal sequenced after a security-relevant baseline, hence SENIOR.

Acceptance: `grep -rn pipelock internal/ --include=*.go` returns nothing; `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./...` green; a `dune logs` invocation path still builds (interim Logs unaffected). Report exactly what was deleted vs already-absent.

tasks.title: Smoke-verify the sbx egress posture against the dune-sbx template
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-4 tasks 1.3, 2.3, 6.2, 6.3 — the empirical end-to-end proof against a real installed `sbx` and the Dune sbx template (ghcr.io/mitchell-wallace/dune-sbx, container/sbx/IMAGE_VERSION), mirroring the sbx-3 smoke lap. This runs after Pipelock removal so it validates the unified end state: no Pipelock + egress governed solely by sbx policy.

Outcome: in an ephemeral sandbox, demonstrate and record: (a) under the non-Open baseline a representative documentation site is BLOCKED (403/denied), and the denial appears in `sbx policy log <instance>`; (b) opening the exact + specific-wildcard domains for that docs site UNBLOCKS it immediately on the running sandbox without recreation, and REMOVING the rule re-blocks it (task 2.3); (c) `sbx policy log` records both shell (forward) and nested-Docker (transparent) traffic; (d) Dune's actual toolchain traffic works under the baseline (npm/pip/go/cargo, AI providers) — record any domains that must be added for parity (task 1.3); (e) no Pipelock sidecar starts and no pipelock.yaml is generated (spec scenario 'No Pipelock in the sbx egress path').

Files & scope: a smoke test/harness consistent with the sbx-3 smoke approach; may shell out to the real sbx. Remove any temporary sandboxes at the end (task 6.3). Build an ephemeral container to test in if needed (permitted by AGENTS.md).

Design: keep the smoke gate honest — if a toolchain domain is missing from Balanced, record it as guidance (kits handle the durable allowlist in sbx-6); do not silently weaken to Open. If `sbx`/template are unavailable in this environment, report that explicitly rather than faking a pass.

Acceptance: the five observations above captured with the actual commands/output; `go build ./cmd/dune` and `go test ./...` green; temp sandboxes removed. Report the recorded toolchain-domain findings for the docs lap.

tasks.title: Document the sbx egress and secrets posture
tasks.description:
Context: sbx-4 task 7.1. Document the posture this change establishes, consistent with the architecture/README docs updated in sbx-3's docs lap.

Outcome: docs describe (1) the egress posture — the non-Open Balanced-derived baseline, that Dune never weakens to Open and never mutates global sbx policy, the verify-only/warn-closed up-time behavior, sandbox-scoped rules (`sbx policy allow/deny network --sandbox <instance> ...`), and opening project domains with exact + specific-wildcard (preferring those over broad catch-alls); (2) egress observability via `sbx policy log <instance>` as the replacement for `dune logs pipelock`, noting `dune logs pipelock` is gone and the final composed `dune logs` lands in sbx-5; (3) the secrets posture — prefer service-identifier secrets, custom secrets are experimental/out-of-lifecycle (manual cleanup caveat), no secrets baked into the template, agent creds in /persist/agent. Fold in any toolchain domains the smoke lap recorded as needed for parity.

Files & scope: the same docs surface sbx-3 updated (README / architecture docs); do not edit openspec change files as docs. Match the existing doc tone/structure.

Acceptance: docs build/render cleanly and a reader can find how to open a domain and where egress logs come from; the Pipelock-is-gone note is present. No code changes.
